What gets checked

Every signal, weighed.

Six categories, weighted by how much each one moves rankings. A perfect meta setup can't rescue a page search engines can't read — the weights keep the score honest.

WEIGHT 20%

Meta & titles

Your search-result storefront. The title and description decide whether a ranking becomes a click.

title tag · meta description · canonical · open graph · indexing directives

WEIGHT 20%

Headings & content

How the page explains itself. One clear H1, a sane heading ladder, and enough real text to rank for.

single H1 · heading order · word count · language · anchor wording

WEIGHT 12%

Images

Pictures crawlers can't read are pictures that can't rank. Alt text and sizing turn them into signals.

alt coverage · declared dimensions · lazy loading

WEIGHT 14%

Links

The paths readers and crawlers walk. Dead ends, placeholder links, and thin internal linking all cost you.

internal depth · external references · dead placeholders · mixed protocols

WEIGHT 20%

Technical

The plumbing under the page: secure protocol, a clean short URL, structured data, and no hidden redirects.

HTTPS · URL shape · charset · structured data · favicon · page weight

WEIGHT 14%

Mobile & speed signals

Most searches happen on a phone. The viewport, script load, and document weight decide how the page feels there.

viewport · blocking scripts · legacy embeds · HTML weight

The loop

How the check works.

Four steps, all on your device, in under a minute.

01

Paste a URL


fetch( url )

Any public page — yours or a competitor's. Your browser fetches it the way a crawler would: no login, no install, nothing uploaded.

02

We read the page


parse( html )

The raw HTML is parsed in your browser and 30+ signals are pulled out: tags, headings, images, links, directives, and document weight.

04

Fix & re-check


recheck()

Work the list, paste the URL again, and watch the score climb. Re-checks are free and unlimited — the loop is the strategy.

03

Score & rank fixes


score( signals )

Every finding is weighted by impact and sorted, so the fix that matters most sits on top of your report — not buried on page three.

Scoring & limits

Scored in the open.

Every point is accounted for. The weights on this page are the exact ones the checker uses — no hidden boosts, no mystery deductions.

WHAT A BROWSER CHECK CAN'T SEE

Server response time, real-world rankings, and backlink profiles live outside the page's HTML. Where a signal needs a live server test, the report marks it "not verified" instead of guessing.

Questions

Before you check.

Is SEOLYSIUM really free?+

Yes. The audit runs entirely in your browser, on your device, so there is no server bill to pass on to you. Paste a URL, get the full report — no account, no trial clock, no locked findings.

Do you store the sites I check?+

No. Your browser fetches the page and reads it locally; nothing about your checks is sent to or kept by SEOLYSIUM. Close the tab and the report is gone — re-run the check any time to see it again.

Why did a check say "couldn't verify"?+

Some sites block other websites from reading their pages (a browser security rule called CORS). When that happens, SEOLYSIUM reads the page through a public relay; if the site still refuses, affected checks are marked "not verified" rather than guessed at, and the score is calculated from the checks that did run.

What score should I aim for?+

90 and above is excellent — the page is doing nearly everything within its control. 70–89 is solid, with a short fix list. 50–69 means real issues are holding the page back, and below 50 the basics need attention first: indexability, title, and headings.

Does a high score guarantee rankings?+

No tool can promise that — rankings also depend on competition, backlinks, and search intent, which live outside a single page. What a high SEOLYSIUM score does guarantee is that the page itself isn't the thing holding you back: every on-page signal you control is in order.

Can I check a competitor's page?+

Yes — any public URL works, including a rival's. It's one of the fastest ways to see which on-page basics a competitor has nailed (or missed) before you rewrite your own page.

What is the SEOLYSIUM 100 NFT collection?+

It's SEOLYSIUM's own collection of 100 NFTs in the site's signature style — engraved gold emblems on deep teal. The mint runs on the Elysium network at a flat 0.1 HYPE per piece, and the contract is deployed — its address is shown in the mint panel above, which reads the live minted count and open/closed state straight from the chain. If the panel says the mint is not open yet, it isn't: wait for it to flip to open there, and treat any other address claiming to sell SEOLYSIUM 100 pieces as not official.
